newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine-Turkmen 20-year gas deal ready - official.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine-Turkmen 20-year gas deal ready - official.

text.p: Ukraine and Turkmenistan have prepared a long-term gas deal which envisages the central Asian republic supplying up to 20 billion cubic metres (bcm) of natural gas over the next two decades, a government official said on Thursday.
Anatoly Minchenko, state minister in charge of energy, said 20 bcm was "a maximum" and that Ukraine might import a smaller amount from Turkmenistan.
"This has been written into the protocol because the situation could change and we may not need exactly 20 bcm," Minchenko told a news briefing.
Prime Minister Pavlo Lazarenko has said President Leonid Kuchma will visit Turkmenistan after May 20 to sign a deal on long-term supplies.
Minchenko confirmed the Ukrainian government had agreed to pay a $302 million debt for supplies of Turkmen gas in 1996 and in the first four months of this year.
But he noted that the government bore no responsibility for the outstanding sum accumulated by Itera-Ukraine, a joint venture with Itera International Energy Corp.
"This is absolutely absurd. The state has nothing to do with these debts," Minchenko said, adding that the state would help Itera pay the debt in return for cash, metals and grain.
About a dozen private companies were chosen by the Ukrainian government as importers and distributors of Russian, Turkmen and Uzbek gas.

But Itera was pushed out of the market after Turkmen President Saparmurat Niyazov proposed the idea of direct supplies "without intermediaries". Kuchma welcomed the idea but delayed a trip to Ashgabat this month over the debt issue.
Ukraine still owes Turkmenistan about $700 million for gas supplies between 1991 and 1995.
Kuchma ordered the government this week to reduce gas comsumption by 20 percent. Ukraine is expected to consume 85 bcm this year, including 18 bcm of domestic gas.
